candidates: GitHub Actions workflow files must include a top-level `permissions:` block that restricts the `GITHUB_TOKEN` to the minimum required scopes (e.g., `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`). Omitting this block grants the token broad default access; every new or modified workflow file should declare permissions explicitly.

Every `uses:` step in GitHub Actions workflow files must pin actions to a full commit SHA rather than a mutable version tag (e.g., use `actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683` instead of `actions/checkout@v4`). This applies equally to GitHub-owned actions and third-party actions. The project already follows this pattern for some actions (e.g., `pnpm/action-setup` is pinned by hash) — apply the same standard consistently.
